items.line: Plants make their own food using a process called photosynthesis.
The plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil.
Inside the leaves, a green pigment called chlorophyll captures energy from the sunlight.
Using this energy, the plant combines the carbon dioxide and water to make sugar.
The plant keeps the sugar for food and releases oxygen into the air.
So, photosynthesis turns sunlight and air into food for the plant and oxygen for us.
Photosynthesis is the process where plants use sunlight to turn simple ingredients into food.
The plant needs six molecules of carbon dioxide and six molecules of water to start the reaction.
With the help of light and chlorophyll, these ingredients combine to create new substances.
The result is glucose, which the plant uses as food, and oxygen gas that it releases.
This equation matters because it shows how plants provide the food we eat and the oxygen we breathe.
So, the chemical equation summarizes how sunlight and water turn air into life.
